findings.text: Mount point marking offers a check and set contract on a directory entry. It reports missing when any ancestor toward the root lacks hash attachment, refuses detached targets and targets carrying a non mountable mark, reports busy when mount state is already present, and otherwise records mount state and reports success.

Mount point marking holds rename synchronization in exclusive mode across the full check and update. Each ancestor is sampled briefly under its own entry lock, then the target is checked and updated under its own entry lock, before the rename hold is released.

Detachment holds exactly for entries that are unhashed and non root. Non mountability holds exactly when a dedicated mark is present in entry flags. Both conditions are evaluated while holding the target entry lock.

Namespace commit transfers a detached mount subtree into its parent namespace in a single publication step. Reserved capacity becomes accounted capacity with the reservation cleared, the subtree becomes visible to lookup, and the namespace change counter advances with a wakeup to poll waiters. Notification tolerates absence of a namespace.

Mounts in a namespace are ordered in a balanced tree by unique numeric identity with cached edge members for smallest and largest entries. Namespace membership is published once per mount. Root mounts of restricted filesystem types also join a visible collection. Joining the tree triggers a notification hook.

A directory entry denotes a mount namespace file only when its operation vector matches the namespace entry operations and the associated inode private operations match the mount namespace operations.

Tree hardening applies to every mount in a subtree. It always adds an access time lock, mirrors read only and device and privilege and execution restrictions into matching lock bits, and additionally locks non root members that are not queued for expiry.

Propagation group identity uses positive allocation on demand. Creation covers a single mount or a whole subtree, undoing earlier allocations in the same request on failure. Cleanup within a bounded range releases identities that are no longer shared.

Mount count reservation enforces a global maximum. It rejects when current usage already reaches the limit and when current plus reserved usage reaches the limit, measures the incoming subtree, rejects when the measurement exceeds remaining capacity, and otherwise adds the measurement to the reservation.

Propagation replicates a source mount across peer groups reachable from a destination. It uses shared mode for the destination group and slave mode elsewhere with shared upgrade where appropriate, skips unsuitable peers and solitary destinations, attaches each replica under the destination mountpoint, collects replicas on a caller list, reserves namespace capacity for each replica, and clears temporary master marks before returning any error.

Tree copying refuses unbindable sources and namespace file roots unless explicitly allowed. Unbindable descendants are skipped or cause failure depending on locked state, namespace file subtrees are skipped, duplicates preserve locked state and expiry linkage and attach under matching duplicated parents at original mountpoints, and any failure discards the whole partial duplicate under hash protection.

Subdirectory testing runs inside a read side critical section with an optimistic rename sequence sample. When the sample is invalidated it retries under an exclusive rename hold, which guarantees progress on deep or concurrently renamed chains.

Ancestor search walks upward from a candidate toward the root and yields the child directly below a claimed ancestor, or nothing when the claim is absent. Identity of the two entries counts as containment without traversal.

A cloned mount carries no internal flag bits and retains only unbindable transient state. Group identity is cleared in slave or private modes and otherwise inherited, with shared mode ensuring non zero identity and shared status. Identifier mapping is shared by reference. Private clones stand alone while other modes join peer and slave collections with master linkage derived from the source.

Identifier mapping lifetime uses reference counting with two global singletons exempt from counting. Acquisition shares the pointer and counts only non singletons. Release drops the count and frees only on last reference of a non singleton. Freeing releases extended forward and reverse tables only when user or group extent counts exceed embedded base capacity.
Mount object teardown releases the identifier mapping reference and deallocates the cover name, device name, per processor counters where present, and the object itself from its dedicated cache.

Group iteration walks peer groups depth first including slave hierarchies and ends at the origin. Replication eligibility excludes freshly created mounts, mounts where the destination is not visible below the root, and mounts in the anonymous namespace. Master selection ascends to a marked or root master and then aligns the replica chain with peer structure.

Mount lookup from a path samples mount sequence state under read side protection and repeats until the result is legitimized. Failed legitimation drops any provisional reference outside the critical section and retries.

Read copy update mount traversal refuses cross device movement when requested, delegates managed entries to a transit handler with directory semantics on specific errors, follows stacked mounts while refreshing path and sequence and validating against concurrent mount mutation, and otherwise reports whether automount handling is required.
Symlink status derives from cached entry type, negative status derives from miss type bits, and managed status derives from the managed mask in entry flags.

Link resolution requires stack capacity and honors trailing and symlink ban restrictions including mount wide bans. It refreshes access time with lazy handling, enforces security policy, obtains content from cache or filesystem handler with unlazy retry, normalizes absolute targets through the filesystem root while collapsing separators, and treats empty content as a pure jump without residual text.

Access time refresh is suppressed for no access time inode marks, unmapped ownership, read only or no access time superblocks, directory specific superblock suppression, mount wide suppressions, equal timestamps, and relative time veto. Relative time mode permits refresh only when modification or status change is not older than access time or when access time is at least a day old.

Access time update revalidates need, attempts filesystem freeze protection without blocking, requires mount write access, delegates to filesystem specific or generic timestamp handling while ignoring timestamp errors on the walk path, and releases protections symmetrically. Generic handling rejects nonblocking updates when a dirty inode handler exists and otherwise propagates dirtiness to the inode.

Dentry and mount control state uses distinct bits for mounted indication and refusal of mounting, for managed transit and automount need, for entry typing covering symlink and miss cases, and for read only and device and privilege and execution and timing and symlink follow restrictions with matching lock variants.

Propagation control uses shared and slave and private and unbindable modes plus transient new and marked states, with positive numeric group identities and copy control distinguishing unbindable and namespace file and shared creation and slave and private and expiry requests.
